luma-evt-P8SOblAuUmAsdt6.summaryLead: A full-day, hands-on workshop in Zürich teaching public administration employees how to work smarter with ChatGPT and other large language models through practical prompt engineering techniques.

sections.heading: What This Workshop Is Actually About
content: Artificial intelligence isn't some abstract concept for Swiss civil servants anymore. It's already showing up in offices across the public sector, and ChatGPT is usually the first tool people encounter. This full-day training at the Technopark in Zürich is built around a simple premise: if you're going to use these tools, you should know how to use them well enough to get real work done.

The session is organized by staatslabor, a Swiss nonprofit whose stated mission is helping the public administration become more innovative and collaborative through new methods and technologies. They're teaming up with AI Bridge, a partner organization that helps institutions prepare for the AI landscape. Together they're running an interactive day of learning that goes beyond surface-level demos.

sections.heading: What You'll Walk Away With
content: The curriculum covers three main areas. First, you'll get a solid grounding in how large language models actually work — not in a way that requires a computer science degree, but enough to understand what these systems can and can't do. That context matters when you're deciding which tasks to hand off to an AI and which ones still need a human eye.

Second, the workshop teaches prompt engineering techniques that go beyond basic queries. You'll practice writing prompts that pull useful, specific answers out of LLMs rather than getting generic output you'd have to rewrite anyway. Third, you apply everything to real administrative scenarios — tasks from your actual workload that could be simplified or sped up with the right approach. The goal isn't to replace judgment; it's to cut down the tedious parts so you can focus on the work that actually matters.

There's also an explicit emphasis on doing all of this within the boundaries of internal guidelines and data protection regulations. Public administration has stricter privacy requirements than most private sector work, and the workshop doesn't ignore that reality.

sections.heading: The Practical Details You Need
content: The workshop runs on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, from 9:15 AM to 5:00 PM at the Technopark in Zürich — specifically at Technoparkstrasse 1, about ten minutes by tram from Zürich Hauptbahnhof. After the formal session wraps up, there's an apéro where participants can meet each other and the staatslabor community informally.

The price is CHF 650 per person, excluding VAT. Payment options include credit card, debit card, or invoice. The course runs with a minimum of 6 and maximum of 20 participants, so it stays small enough for genuine interaction. Spots are filled on a first-come, first-served basis, and the page notes that only one spot remained at time of writing.

sections.heading: Who This Is For (and Who It Isn't)
content: This workshop is exclusively for employees of public administration. Staatslabor reserves the right to reject registrations from people who don't meet that criteria, so don't sign up if you're in the private sector hoping for a nice day out in Zürich.

Every registration is binding and commits you to paying the course fee. If you can't make it, you need to inform staatslabor proactively before the program starts. If the minimum enrollment isn't met, the course gets canceled and fees are fully refunded. It's straightforward, no-nonsense terms — which honestly tracks for a program run by and for the Swiss public sector.

luma-host-evt-u8z3itUrY0D0LaN.summaryLead: Light DAO's monthly virtual town hall brings together 7,000+ conscious entrepreneurs and 1,200+ investors from 16 cities worldwide for ecosystem updates, a beta app launch, and breakout room connections.

sections.heading: Who Light DAO Actually Is
content: Light DAO describes itself as a global community of conscious entrepreneurs and investors. That word 'conscious' is doing real work in their mission statement — they're focused on what they call expanding collective consciousness and co-creating a regenerative future for humanity. Whether that language resonates with you or makes you skeptical probably depends on where you sit, but the numbers behind it are concrete: over 7,000 entrepreneurs and 1,200 investors across 16 cities in North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia.

This isn't a crypto bro operation running on vibes alone. They have a structured membership system with two tiers — Dao Guest access for qualified investors and experienced founders, and Dao Member Owner status that grants access to both virtual and in-person gatherings across their 16-city network.

sections.heading: What's on the September Agenda
content: The September 9 town hall has a packed agenda. They're opening with a global ecosystem overview, which means updates on what's happening across their various city chapters and initiatives. Then there's a rundown of upcoming gatherings and community events — essentially a calendar preview so members know what's coming.

The headline item is the beta launch of the Light app, which is clearly something the organization has been building toward. Beyond that, there's a stewardship overview, presentations from mastermind teams that focus on deeper collaboration, and global member highlights that spotlight what people in the network are actually building. The session closes with a group connection experience in breakout rooms, which sounds like the structured networking portion where attendees get paired for focused conversations.
The whole thing runs from 6:00 to 7:00 PM on a single evening, keeping it tight. For a monthly recurring event, that brevity is smart — it respects people's time while still covering a lot of ground.

sections.heading: Membership Tiers and Access
content: Getting into the town hall requires either Dao Guest or Dao Member Owner registration, and both tiers require approval. Guest access is for qualified investors and experienced founders, while Member Owner status opens up the full range of Light DAO gatherings — virtual and in-person — across all 16 cities.

At the time of writing, 41 people were already registered as going, with names like Patrick Meagher and Evan Arteaga among them. The approval process suggests they're curating the room deliberately, which makes sense for a community built around 'conscious' entrepreneurship. They're not trying to fill a stadium; they're building a network with specific criteria.

sections.heading: The Virtual Format and Global Reach
content: Holding the town hall virtually makes sense for an organization that spans six continents. A single in-person event in any one city would exclude most of the network, so the virtual format is essentially the only way to get everyone in the same room simultaneously.

The breakout room component is the interesting part — virtual networking at scale is notoriously difficult, but structured breakout sessions at least create the conditions for real one-on-one or small-group conversations. Whether those conversations turn into meaningful collaborations is up to the participants, but the format gives them a fighting chance.

luma-evt-mBERNwQdX2gmBia.summaryLead: A 45-minute strength and endurance fitness class in Los Angeles that pairs functional training with community — plus a complimentary cafecito from Ülew for every attendee.

sections.heading: The Class Itself
content: This isn't a CrossFit gauntlet or a boutique cycling class with a DJ. It's a 45-minute strength and endurance session designed for all fitness levels, focused on functional movements — the kind that make carrying groceries, climbing stairs, and playing with your kids easier. The emphasis is on building real-world strength, improving cardio endurance, and getting people to leave feeling more capable than when they arrived.

Hosted by Metztli Garcia in Los Angeles, the class explicitly invites all levels. Whether you're someone who's never lifted a weight or you're a regular gym-goer looking for a different format, the framing is the same: show up, move your body, and feel stronger afterward. There's no mention of specific equipment or advanced requirements, which keeps the barrier to entry low. The workout targets both strength and endurance in a single session, which means you're not just lifting heavy things or just running on a treadmill — you're getting a balanced push that tests multiple energy systems in under an hour.

sections.heading: Community as the Main Event
content: Here's what makes this different from booking a class at your local gym: after the workout, everyone gets a cafecito from Ülew included with their ticket. The host explicitly calls out that building community is just as important as building muscle. That framing matters — this isn't a transaction where you pay for exercise and leave. It's structured to create social connection around a shared physical activity. The coffee isn't an afterthought either — it's baked into the ticket price, which means nobody has to awkwardly split a check or wonder whether the host is expecting them to buy their own drink.

The invitation to bring your bestie is part of that same ethos. The event name — 'Strong Looks Good On You, Bestie!' — sets a tone that's encouraging rather than competitive. In a fitness culture that often leans into intensity and transformation narratives, this one leans into warmth and belonging. It's a small detail, but the choice to frame the event around friendship and mutual support rather than competition or personal records tells you something about the kind of environment Metztli Garcia is trying to build.

sections.heading: Logistics and the Waitlist Situation
content: The event is already full. At the time of the listing, 25 people were marked as going, and the registration page offered a waitlist option. If additional spots open up, people on the waitlist get notified. That demand signals real interest in what Metztli Garcia is building.

The cost is $15, payable via Venmo or Zelle (with a specific Zelle tag: boyleheightsbestie). Payment is required before approval — no payment, no registration confirmed. The exact class location in Los Angeles is only revealed after registration, which is a common approach for pop-up fitness events to manage capacity and prevent overcrowding.

sections.heading: Refund Policy and Fine Print
content: Refunds are accepted only if requested at least 48 hours before the event starts. After that window closes, your payment is locked in. It's a simple policy that protects the organizer from last-minute drop-offs while still giving people a reasonable grace period to change their minds.

For $15, this is about as low-risk a social experiment as you can find. You get a workout, a coffee, and a room full of people in Los Angeles who are interested in fitness and community. Whether that turns into lasting friendships or just a good Saturday morning is entirely up to what you make of it.

luma-evt-Dd3eNd55rFmR8bj.summaryLead: A multi-day beginner acting workshop at HAFA Art Studio in Fountain Valley covering camera and theater fundamentals, scene study, and character development — culminating in a certificate and potential casting opportunities.

sections.heading: What the Workshop Covers
content: This is a beginner-level acting workshop spread across six days, totaling 24 hours of instruction. The curriculum is split between acting for camera and acting for theater — two disciplines that share a root but demand very different skills. You'll work through scene study and character development, which means understanding how to break down a script, find a character's motivation, and deliver a performance that feels grounded rather than theatrical.

The workshop is a joint presentation by three organizations: HAFA Art Studio, Starz Studio by Marwa Gabriel, and I Studio by Rafik El Rihany. The involvement of the Hollywood Arab Film Festival/Association (HAFA) as the hosting body connects this workshop to a broader network in the Arab film community. That connection pays off at the end — participants will be considered for future casting opportunities through Starz by Marwa Gabriel, giving the training a direct pathway to professional work. It's not just education for its own sake — there's a tangible professional outcome attached to completion.

sections.heading: The Schedule and Where It Happens
content: The workshop runs from September 14 through September 19, 2026. Monday through Friday sessions run from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM, and Saturday wraps up with an 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM session. That structure lets working people attend the evening sessions without quitting their day jobs, while the Saturday session provides a natural closing experience. The evening format also mirrors real-world filming and rehearsal schedules, which tend to run late — getting used to performing after a full day of other activities is a useful skill in itself.

All sessions take place at HAFA Art Studio, located at 18386 Brookhurst Street in Fountain Valley, California (ZIP code 92708). Fountain Valley sits in Orange County, about 35 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles. The studio setting means a more intimate learning environment compared to a large theater or university classroom. For beginners who might feel intimidated by a big institutional space, a studio environment tends to feel more personal and less like you're being graded.

sections.heading: Language and Accessibility
content: The instruction is delivered in English with Arabic support available. That bilingual approach reflects the workshop's roots in the Arab film community and makes the training accessible to a wider range of participants. For Arabic-speaking aspiring actors in Southern California, this removes a significant barrier that often exists in English-dominant acting programs.

Every participant who completes the workshop receives a Certificate of Completion presented by all three partner organizations. It's not just a participation trophy — the certificate is backed by three distinct studios and the Hollywood Arab Film Festival, which gives it weight if you're building a resume or applying to other programs.

sections.heading: Registration, Pricing, and What to Know Before You Sign Up
content: Registration comes with two pricing tiers. Early Bird through August 16 costs $400, and regular registration from August 17 through September 14 is $600. Both tiers are non-refundable and non-transferable, so make sure the dates work before committing. At the time of listing, 14 people were registered and only 2 spots remained. The sharp price jump between early and regular registration — a 50 percent increase — makes a clear case for committing early if you know this is something you want to do.

Spots are filled on a first-come, first-served basis with no waitlist mentioned, which means when they're gone, they're gone. If you're considering this workshop, the early bird pricing saves you $200 and disappears a month before the workshop starts. The combination of 24 hours of instruction, a certificate from three studios, and a pathway to casting considerations makes the $400 early bird price a strong value for serious beginners. For context, a single private acting lesson in Los Angeles typically runs $75 to $150 per hour, so getting 24 hours of group instruction with three studio partners for $400 is a different proposition entirely.

luma-evt-aQiimIN6V6gLF9o.summaryLead: A three-hour program at MIT exploring how AI is reshaping cinema — featuring curated film screenings, filmmaker discussions, industry panels, and networking in Cambridge, Massachusetts on Halloween night.

sections.heading: What This Festival Is
content: The Boston — Silicon Valley AI Film Festival is an extension of an international platform dedicated to the intersection of artificial intelligence and filmmaking. This regional edition, scheduled for October 31, 2026, brings together filmmakers, AI creators, tech innovators, researchers, startup founders, investors, students, and creative professionals for a focused three-hour program at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

The event is hosted by Boston International Media Consulting, Inc. (BIMC), and co-hosted by two MIT student organizations: the Asian Women Development Association (AWDA) and Asian Women Development Plan International (AWDPI). The partnership between a media consulting firm and two MIT student associations reflects the event's dual nature — it's both an industry gathering and an academic exploration of where AI-powered storytelling is heading.

sections.heading: The Program Breakdown
content: The three-hour structure is packed. It opens with remarks, then moves into a curated showcase of AI-assisted and AI-generated films. This isn't a free-for-all screening — the films are selected, which means a curatorial team has decided what's worth showing and in what order. After the showcase, the format shifts to industry panels and roundtable discussions with filmmakers and technology professionals.

An audience Q&A gives attendees direct access to the people making and thinking about AI film. There are also creative-technology presentations or demonstrations, which could range from live AI filmmaking tools to behind-the-scenes looks at production workflows. The program closes with structured networking, giving the 35+ registered attendees a chance to connect with each other and with the featured speakers.

sections.heading: The Topics on the Table
content: The festival explicitly covers a wide range of topics that reflect where the AI-film conversation currently sits. Generative AI and visual storytelling is the big umbrella, but underneath that are more specific threads: AI filmmaking tools and production workflows, emerging video-generation technologies, the tension between human creativity and machine-assisted creation, and the thorny questions around authorship, intellectual property, and responsible AI use.

There's also attention paid to entrepreneurship and innovation in creative technology, plus cross-cultural storytelling in the AI era. That last topic connects to the co-hosts' focus and the international scope of the broader Silicon Valley AI Film Festival. It's not just about what AI can do technically — it's about who gets to tell stories and how cultural perspectives shape the technology.

sections.heading: The Venue and Logistics
content: The event takes place at MIT's campus at 77 Massachusetts Avenue in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The exact room within MIT hasn't been announced yet — registration details and the specific location are noted as forthcoming. The timing on October 31 puts it in the middle of Tough Tech Week, a detail the listing highlights. That scheduling positions the festival within a broader ecosystem of technology and innovation events happening around Boston that week.

The event runs from 2:00 to 5:00 PM EDT, which is early enough that you still have your Halloween evening free. At the time of writing, 35 people were registered as going, with names like Herve Flutto from Sparksense and Prajakta Kalbande among them. Registration is currently open with no mention of a fee, though that could change as the event approaches.

sections.heading: Who Should Show Up
content: This event is most valuable for people who sit at the intersection of film and technology — not just filmmakers curious about AI, and not just technologists curious about film, but people who are actively working at that boundary. If you're building AI tools for video, making films that use generative technology, researching the ethical implications, or investing in creative tech startups, this room has something for you.

The MIT location also makes it accessible to students and researchers who might not have the budget for expensive industry conferences but want to engage with the AI-film conversation. The networking component, with 35+ attendees and panel participants from Sparksense and other organizations, provides the kind of face-to-face connection that's hard to replicate online. And it's free — or at least it's listed without a fee at this stage.
